DETERMINISTIC_PROOF.one_of_my_own_expectations_was_wrong_and: I predicted repeat apply would refuse on the emitted-output collision. It refuses EARLIER, on the already-bound Job, because apply rehearses before it writes. That ordering is the better one -- 'this Job already exists' is a stronger statement than 'a file is in the way' -- so the check now asserts the real ordering and the output-collision ordering is exercised separately, before the apply, where it is reachable.
DETERMINISTIC_PROOF.limits: Scenario 1 is read-only measurement of the real instance. Scenario 2 is disposable with a SIMULATED repository runner and a STUB bundle, and its retained Job was configured but never ran. That the new Job will SUCCEED is not proved -- only that it is configured, bound, collision-free and selectable.
